label: Myth vs. Fact

slides.title: 4 anesthesia myths that trip up students
slides.sub: How many did you believe in your first semester?

slides.myth: A good pulse ox means the patient is ventilating.
slides.fact: SpO2 shows oxygenation. On high FiO2 it can stay normal while CO2 climbs. Capnography shows ventilation.
Sugammadex binds rocuronium and vecuronium. It does not reverse succinylcholine.

slides.myth: A higher MAC means a stronger volatile agent.
slides.fact: It's the opposite. A lower MAC means a more potent agent.
slides.pearl: MAC = the concentration that stops movement to incision in 50% of patients.

slides.myth: Any BP cuff size gives you a good reading.
slides.fact: Too small reads falsely high. Too large reads falsely low. Size the cuff to the arm.

label: Common Mistakes

slides.title: 5 mistakes new anesthesia students make in clinicals
slides.sub: Number 4 costs students hours at the end of every semester.

slides.mistake: Walking in without checking the room
slides.why: The patient is on the table and the suction isn't on.
slides.fix: Do the machine check and turn on the suction in every room, every case.

slides.mistake: Drawing up a drug and labeling it later
slides.why: Unlabeled syringes are how swaps happen.
slides.fix: Label every syringe the moment you draw it up.

slides.why: You recognize it on paper and freeze in the OR.
slides.fix: Review 20 minutes a day, and say the 'why' out loud.

slides.mistake: Logging cases at the end of the week
slides.why: Details fade and your case counts end up wrong.
slides.fix: Log every case the same day, right after the shift.

slides.why: It tells your preceptor you haven't thought it through.
slides.fix: Come with your plan, then ask: 'Here's my plan. What would you change?'

slides.title: Which one have you done?
slides.body: Our clinical logbooks and student planner make #3 and #4 easy.

label: Comparison

slides.title: Phenylephrine vs. ephedrine
slides.sub: Two pressors students mix up all the time. Here's the simple version.

rows: Low BP with a normal or high HR
Low BP with a low HR

slides.big: Look at the heart rate first.
bullets: HR high or normal: phenylephrine
HR low: ephedrine
slides.pearl: Always treat the cause too: depth, volume, position, surgical field.

slides.title: Pressors, simplified.
slides.body: Our medication study cards break every drug down like this.

caption:
BP drops after induction. Phenylephrine or ephedrine? Check the heart rate first. 💉

Phenylephrine is a direct alpha-1 agonist that can slow the HR, so it fits low BP with a normal or fast HR. Ephedrine works mostly indirectly with alpha and beta effects and tends to raise the HR, so it fits low BP with a slow HR. And always treat the cause.

label: Checklist

slides.title: Room setup before every induction
slides.sub: Remember SOAP-ME. Screenshot it and run it every morning.

items: On, working, and within reach of the head
Machine check done, backup O2 cylinder and a self-inflating bag ready
Mask, oral and nasal airways, laryngoscopes that light up, tubes, stylet, plus your backup plan
Induction drugs, relaxant, pressors and emergency drugs drawn up and labeled
ECG, BP cuff sized right, SpO2, capnography, temperature
IV running, warmer, bed controls, padding and positioning gear
slides.pearl: If anything is missing, the patient waits. Not the other way around.

label: Step-by-Step

slides.title: Rapid sequence induction in 6 steps
slides.sub: The order matters. Here's the sequence, one step at a time.

slides.title: Prepare
bullets: Suction on, under the pillow
Plan A, B and C said out loud
Drugs drawn up and labeled

slides.title: Preoxygenate
bullets: Tight mask seal, 100% O2
Aim for an end-tidal O2 of about 90%

slides.title: Induce and paralyze
bullets: Give the hypnotic, then the relaxant right after
Cricoid pressure per your institution's practice

slides.title: Minimize mask ventilation
bullets: Gentle, low-pressure breaths only if needed to prevent desaturation

slides.title: Intubate and cuff up
bullets: Inflate the cuff before ventilating

slides.title: Confirm placement
bullets: Sustained ETCO2 waveform
Bilateral breath sounds and chest rise

slides.title: Prepare. Preoxygenate. Push. Place. Prove.

label: Unpopular Opinion

slides.title: Memorizing doses isn't the hard part of anesthesia school
slides.sub: Here's what actually separates students who struggle from students who don't.

slides.quote: The hard part is knowing WHY the patient is doing what they're doing.
slides.sub: Doses you can look up. Reasoning you can't.

bullets: If you know the mechanism, you can predict the problem before the monitor does
Anticipating beats reacting
Preceptors trust students who can explain their plan
For every drug, ask: what will it do to BP, HR and breathing?
After every case, write one thing that surprised you
Map how topics connect, not just what they are
slides.pearl: Understanding sticks. Memorized lists fade after the exam.
